author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ford is recalling 223,472 F-150 pickup trucks in the United States because fuel tanks may leak or separate from the vehicle while it is moving, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The action covers certain trucks from model years 2023 through 2027.

The safety agency said some tanks may be improperly secured. A detached tank can become a road hazard and increase crash risk, while leaking fuel can cause an engine stall or create a fire risk. The notice does not mean every truck in the model-year range has the defect; owners will be notified based on the vehicles included in Ford’s recall population.

Dealers will inspect the fuel-tank straps and replace them when necessary at no charge, NHTSA said. Owners should use their vehicle identification number with the federal recall database or contact a Ford dealer to determine whether a specific truck is affected and to arrange service after notices are issued. The recall highlights how a relatively basic mounting component can create several connected safety problems, from loss of propulsion to debris on the road and exposure to leaking fuel.
dek: Certain 2023-2027 F-150 trucks may have leaking or improperly secured tanks that can stall an engine, create a road hazard or raise fire risk.
headline: Ford recalls 223,472 F-150 trucks over fuel-tank risk
